hypothesis: RUNTIME surface: meter every real provider HTTP call (success AND failure) into a per-vault monthly-sharded append-only ledger `.ovp/usage/llm-usage-YYYY-MM.jsonl`, at the innermost client point (`AnthropicBlockingClient.with_usage_ledger`, one HTTP = one row, so retry-internal attempts and the first BudgetExhausted are visible), plus a read-only `ovp2 usage` command (day x lane rollup, soft daily_token_budget warn from `.ovp/providers.toml` `[budget]`) and token estimates on `source-work backfill --dry-run`. Predicted: operators can see per-day token spend per lane (today: zero visibility), estimate batch cost before enqueueing, and get an 80%/100% warn when the day exceeds a configured soft budget — with ZERO behavior change to any existing command (metering is a side channel that can never fail the call; unwired call sites are explicitly unmetered and labeled as such).

predicted_delta.metering_completeness: 100% of wired live HTTP exchanges produce exactly one ledger row (retries and budget-exhausted first attempts included); 0 rows from replay/offline runs and 0 rows from explicitly unwired call sites; a day with N wired live calls shows N rows summed across that day's shard
predicted_delta.operational_reliability: the 2026-08 network-outage/backfill-blowout class of incident becomes visible in numbers (tokens/day/lane, failure counts) instead of anecdote; budget overruns warn same-day instead of at the invoice; backfill dry-run answers 'how much will this cost' before enqueueing hundreds of items
predicted_delta.coverage: no portal/coverage surface changes — this candidate is observability-only by operator decision (meter, do not enforce)

guardrails.side_channel_never_fails_call: a ledger write failure (disk full, unwritable dir, shard creation) logs to stderr ONCE and is never propagated into `call()` — the LLM path behaves byte-identically with metering on or off; test: unwritable ledger path → call still returns Ok
guardrails.opt_in_and_replay_silent: metering only exists where `.with_usage_ledger(path)` is explicitly wired (server ask/worker clients + vault-aware build_client call sites); `None` = zero overhead, zero files; replay/offline clients never touch the ledger, offline determinism and cassette-replay CI untouched
guardrails.honest_failure_rows: rows for calls that failed WITH a response body carry the real token counts (read from the raw body in `call()`, `parse_anthropic_reply` untouched); transport failures record null tokens, never fabricated zeros
guardrails.no_callerror_change: `CallError` (29 construction sites, PartialEq+Serialize with whole-value asserts) is not modified; metering lives inside AnthropicBlockingClient only
guardrails.providers_toml_forward_compat: `ProvidersFile` gains `#[serde(default)] budget` and DROPS top-level `deny_unknown_fields` so a `[budget]`-bearing file never breaks older binaries reading the same vault (desktop sidecar, scheduler-spawned binaries); format/type errors stay fail-loud
guardrails.read_only_reporting: `ovp2 usage` never deletes anything (rotation happens write-side, monthly shards, >90d pruned on first write of a new month); `ovp2 usage --days N` cannot conflict with pruning

eval_plan.replay_set: unit tests, no live calls: (1) record_usage pure function: ok row / body-failure row with real tokens / transport row with null tokens / unwritable path never errors; (2) ledger absent builder → zero side effects, replay client → no shard file; (3) ProvidersFile: [budget] parses via the same loader, unknown sections tolerated, malformed toml still Err, missing file → default; (4) aggregation: hand-written shard fixtures → day x lane totals, budget threshold warns, cross-month reads, write-side pruning; (5) dry-run estimate: with-history uses lane averages, cold-start uses labeled upper-bound constants

rollback: Single revert: metering is an un-wired builder (None = no code path), ProvidersFile fields are serde-default additive, `ovp2 usage` is read-only. Deleting `.ovp/usage/` removes all recorded data with no other effect.
